description: Cases for the canonical session duration. Kotlin SessionTimeReconciler.canonicalDurationMillis and Dart sessionDurationMillis both read this file, so a failure states that the rule moved rather than that one language moved first. The duration is derived, never stored, which is why a synced row needs this rule at all. Expected values are derived by hand from the rules, not captured from either implementation.

cases.name: the monotonic clock answers when both ends share a boot
cases.why: 1440 s of elapsed realtime. The wall clock agrees and is not consulted.

cases.name: a wall clock that stepped does not overrule the monotonic clock
cases.why: The same 1440 s of elapsed time, with a wall clock that jumped back an hour mid-drive. Without this rule the drive lasts minus twenty minutes.

cases.name: a span across two boots falls back to the wall clock
cases.why: Elapsed realtime restarts at a reboot, so the monotonic delta measures nothing. The wall clock is what is left, and it is inside the band.

cases.name: a row with no boot count falls back to the wall clock
cases.why: Rows recorded before the car stamped the boot count. The monotonic delta cannot be trusted without knowing the two ends share a boot.

cases.name: a wall span past the cap is a corrupt stamp, not a long drive
cases.why: Two boots, so the monotonic clock is out, and a wall span of 60 h against a 48 h cap. Null, so a reader prints a dash instead of a drive that lasted two and a half days.

cases.name: a negative wall span is refused
cases.why: The wall clock stepped back across a reboot, so neither clock can answer.

cases.name: a charge may last days, and the cap says so
cases.why: The same 60 h wall span that is refused for a drive is an ordinary week of sitting plugged in.

cases.name: an unstamped elapsed start cannot carry a monotonic span
cases.why: A zero elapsed stamp is an absent one, not the instant the car booted.
